claim: On Xiaohongshu, slowed-down dance tutorials are a whole content category — 6,909 likes, 4,667, 2,979, 2,727 — and every single one exists only because a teacher was willing to re-dance that song by hand. The commenters say exactly why: at that speed, they believe they can learn it. There is a Chinese word for the labour behind this (扒舞) and one of the platform's own search suggestions is 扒舞好累啊 — 'reverse-engineering choreography is exhausting'.
method: Applied the only sourcing move that worked twice this week — hunt for high-engagement manual how-to tutorials, because a popular tutorial is proof the product does not exist — to a mass consumer scene instead of a craft niche. Searched Xiaohongshu for 求分解 镜像 舞蹈 / 扒舞 / 求慢速分解 / 跳舞镜像分不清左右 / 扒舞app推荐, read the comment sections of the highest-engagement posts, then checked what the existing 扒舞 apps actually do.
does: Drop in one dance video you found yourself, and 30 seconds later get the version you can actually practise to: segmented into eight-counts along the music, each segment at half speed, one plain-language cue per count ('left hand to chest, right foot points forward'), and a printable move list. Version two opens the camera and tells you which eight-count you got wrong.
edge: Every tool in this space is a video player. This one reads the movement — which is what makes eight-count segmentation, spoken cues and error-spotting possible at all.
why_use: Because whether an ordinary person can learn a dance at all is decided by speed and segmentation, and today that depends entirely on whether some teacher happened to hand-produce a slow version of that specific song. If nobody did, you stop.
gap: The existing 扒舞 apps are speed / mirror / frame-step / loop players — 终于有工具可以逐帧练舞了 (354 likes), 小众APP｜跳舞人必备扒舞APP (412), plus individuals building their own (习舞一年，我做了一个新手练舞专用 App). Not one of them understands what is happening in the frame: no automatic eight-count splitting, no cues, no feedback on your own body, and none of them can produce the back-facing view everybody actually wants. Mirroring is one line of code and was never the hard part — mirroring flips the clothes, the room and the face too, which is precisely why teachers film a separate back-view take.
counter: Douyin and Kuaishou sit on both the videos and the pose models and could ship speed + segmentation as a player feature. Cue generation is the real risk: say 'left' when it is right and you are worse than useless, because this audience trains by muscle memory and a wrong move takes longer to unlearn than to learn. And back-view synthesis from a single camera is still research, so version one must not promise it.
differentiator: Do not build another player — build the thing a teacher does by hand: cut to the eight-count, slow it, and say out loud what the body does on each count, with every cue clickable back to its own frame and left blank rather than guessed when the model is unsure. Local-only on a video the user already found; never host, never redistribute. Cold start (Chinese): the comment sections under the slow-tutorial posts themselves (6,909 / 4,667 / 2,979 / 2,727 likes) are full of people asking for a slow version of one specific song, plus the notes that land on the searches 扒舞好累啊 and 什么app比较适合扒舞. Cold start (English): the 'mirrored version please' comments under YouTube dance tutorials, and r/kpophelp.
value: People learning a dance alone from a phone — from K-pop covers to wedding first dances to square dancing. They pay per dance broken down, or a small subscription once they are learning one a month. The teachers who currently hand-make slow versions are the second market: it collapses a day of work into minutes.
risk: Cue accuracy. A wrong left/right does more damage than no cue at all.

consumer_angle: Someone learning a dance alone from a phone, with no teacher and no studio; the deliverable is that specific dance cut into eight-counts, slowed, and narrated one count at a time.

zh.claim: 小红书上「慢速版」是一个完整的内容品类——6909赞、4667赞、2979赞、2727赞——而每一支的存在，都只是因为有位老师肯为这首歌手工重跳一遍。评论区把因果说得比我们准：到了这个速度，他们觉得自己学得会。这件事在中文里有专门的词（扒舞），而平台自己的搜索联想词之一就是「扒舞好累啊」。
zh.does: 丢进一条你自己找到的舞蹈视频，30 秒后拿到能真正跟着练的那个版本：按音乐切成八拍、每段 0.5 倍速、每一拍一句人话口令（「左手抬到胸口、右脚前点」），外加一份可打印的动作清单。第二版打开摄像头，告诉你第几个八拍跳错了。
zh.edge: 这个领域现有的东西全是播放器。这一个看得懂动作——正因为看得懂，切八拍、给口令、挑错才成立。
zh.why_use: 因为一个普通人学不学得会一支舞，是被速度和分段决定的；而今天这两样存不存在，完全取决于有没有哪位老师刚好为这支歌手工做过慢速版。没有，你就停在那儿。
zh.gap: 现存的扒舞 App 全是变速／镜像／逐帧／循环的播放器——「终于有工具可以逐帧练舞了」354赞、「小众APP｜跳舞人必备扒舞APP」412赞，还有人自己做（「习舞一年，我做了一个新手练舞专用 App」）。没有一个看得懂画面里发生了什么：不会自动切八拍、不给口令、不会看你自己的身体，更给不出所有人真正在等的背面视角。左右翻转只要一行代码，从来不是难点——镜像会把衣服、房间、脸一起翻过去，这正是老师宁可专门再录一遍背面的原因。
zh.counter: 抖音和快手同时握着视频和姿态模型，把变速＋分段做成播放器功能随时可以。真正的风险在口令：说反一次左右就比不给还糟，因为这批人靠肌肉记忆，错动作练进去要花更久改回来。而单目视频合成背面视角仍属研究阶段，所以第一版绝不能承诺它。
zh.differentiator: 别再做播放器，做老师手工在做的那件事：切到八拍、放慢、把每一拍身体在干什么说出来；每条口令都能点回它自己那一帧，机器不确定就留空而不是硬猜。只在本机处理用户自己找到的视频，永不托管、永不再分发。冷启动（中文）：那几条慢速教程本身的评论区（6909／4667／2979／2727赞）挤满了在求某一支歌慢速版的人，再加「扒舞好累啊」「什么app比较适合扒舞」两个搜索词落地的笔记；冷启动（英文）：YouTube dance tutorial 底下常年的 mirrored version please，以及 r/kpophelp。
zh.value: 对着手机一个人学舞的人——从女团翻跳到婚礼舞到广场舞。按「拆解一支舞」付费，一个月学一支之后转小额订阅。现在手工做慢速版的老师是第二个市场：把一天的活压成几分钟。
zh.risk: 口令的准确度。说反一次左右，比什么都不说更糟。
